subject: Life Skills
title: Emotional Granularity
description: A short lesson to help you apply Emotional Granularity.

hook.text: Most people say 'I feel bad.' Psychologist Lisa Feldman Barrett says that vagueness makes the feeling harder to fix.

buildup.text: Emotional granularity means labeling feelings precisely. Not just 'bad' but disappointed, embarrassed, or overwhelmed.

discovery.text: Brain scans show that naming an emotion precisely reduces its intensity. The label itself is a regulation tool.

twist.text: People with high granularity handle stress better and drink less.

climax.text: Build your vocabulary. Replace 'stressed' with specific words: pressured, rushed, uncertain. Precision brings relief.

punchline.text: Name it precisely and the feeling loses its grip.

quiz.question: How does naming an emotion precisely help?
options: It makes the emotion disappear immediately
It reduces the emotion's intensity and improves self-regulation
It helps others understand your feelings better
